# google_sql_blue_green_deployment

A BlueGreenDeployment resource represents a Cloud SQL blue-green deployment setup.


To get more information about BlueGreenDeployment, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/admin-api/rest/v1/projects.locations.blueGreenDeployments)
* How-to Guides
    * [Blue-green deployments overview](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/blue-green-deployments-overview)

~> **Note:** In the `google-beta` provider, `google_sql_database_instance` authoritatively manages
the instance's blue-green deployment through its `blue_green_deployment` block. If the
source instance is managed by Terraform, add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [blue_green_deployment] }`
to it; otherwise Terraform will plan to remove the block and delete this deployment.

## Example Usage - Sql Blue Green Deployment Basic


```hcl
resource "google_sql_database_instance" "source" {
  provider         = google-beta
  name             = "my-instance"
  region           = "us-central1"
  database_version = "MYSQL_8_0"
  settings {
    tier = "db-n1-standard-1"
    backup_configuration {
      enabled            = true
      binary_log_enabled = true
    }
  }
  deletion_protection = false

  # The blue-green deployment is managed by google_sql_blue_green_deployment instead.
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [blue_green_deployment]
  }
}

resource "google_sql_blue_green_deployment" "default" {
  provider                 = google-beta
  blue_green_deployment_id = "my-deployment"
  location                 = "us-central1"
  source_instance          = google_sql_database_instance.source.name
  description              = "Terraform basic blue green deployment test"
}
```

## Example Usage - Sql Blue Green Deployment Requested Config


```hcl
resource "google_sql_database_instance" "source" {
  provider         = google-beta
  name             = "my-instance"
  region           = "us-central1"
  database_version = "MYSQL_8_0"
  settings {
    tier = "db-n1-standard-1"
    backup_configuration {
      enabled            = true
      binary_log_enabled = true
    }
  }
  deletion_protection = false

  # The blue-green deployment is managed by google_sql_blue_green_deployment instead.
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [blue_green_deployment]
  }
}

resource "google_sql_blue_green_deployment" "default" {
  provider                 = google-beta
  blue_green_deployment_id = "my-deployment"
  location                 = "us-central1"
  source_instance          = google_sql_database_instance.source.name
  description              = "Terraform blue green deployment with requested config"
  requested_config {
    database_version = "MYSQL_8_4"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `source_instance` -
  (Required)
  The source Cloud SQL instance (the "blue" instance) for the deployment.
  Accepts either the instance name or the full resource name (projects/{project}/instances/{instance}).

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location in which the blue-green deployment will be created in.

* `blue_green_deployment_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID to use for the blue-green deployment, which will become the final component of the deployment's resource name.


* `description` -
  (Optional)
  User-provided description for the deployment.

* `requested_config` -
  (Optional)
  The configuration intended for the target instance(s) when the deployment was created.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_requested_config).

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_requested_config"></a>The `requested_config` block supports:

* `database_version` -
  (Optional)
  The target database major version for the upgrade. For example, MYSQL_8_0.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/blueGreenDeployments/{{blue_green_deployment_id}}`

* `name` -
  The full resource name of the deployment.
  Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/blueGreenDeployments/{deployment_id}

* `create_time` -
  The time when the deployment was created.

* `state` -
  The current state of the blue-green deployment.

* `switchover_target_instance` -
  The full resource name of the primary target instance (the "green" instance) that will be promoted during switchover.

* `error_detail` -
  Provides details on why switchover is not possible.

* `deployment_mappings` -
  A list representing the pairs of source and target instances in the deployment.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_deployment_mappings).

* `deployment_tasks` -
  Combined list of tasks for all paired nodes in the deployment.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_deployment_tasks).


<a name="nested_deployment_mappings"></a>The `deployment_mappings` block contains:

* `source` -
  (Output)
  Details about the source instance.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_deployment_mappings_source).

* `target` -
  (Output)
  Details about the target instance.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_deployment_mappings_target).

* `state` -
  (Output)
  The state of this specific source-target pair.

* `diffs` -
  (Output)
  Describes the list of differences for the SourceTargetPairedNode.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_deployment_mappings_diffs).


<a name="nested_deployment_mappings_source"></a>The `source` block contains:

* `instance` -
  (Output)
  The full resource name of the instance.

* `connection` -
  (Output)
  The instance connection name.

* `dns` -
  (Output)
  The unique DNS name for this instance.

* `ip_mappings` -
  (Output)
  The list of IP addresses for this instance.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_deployment_mappings_source_ip_mappings).


<a name="nested_deployment_mappings_source_ip_mappings"></a>The `ip_mappings` block contains:

* `ip_address` -
  (Output)
  The IP address assigned.

* `type` -
  (Output)
  The type of this IP address.

* `time_to_retire` -
  (Output)
  The due time for this IP to be retired.

<a name="nested_deployment_mappings_target"></a>The `target` block contains:

* `instance` -
  (Output)
  The full resource name of the instance.

* `connection` -
  (Output)
  The instance connection name.

* `dns` -
  (Output)
  The unique DNS name for this instance.

* `ip_mappings` -
  (Output)
  The list of IP addresses for this instance.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_deployment_mappings_target_ip_mappings).


<a name="nested_deployment_mappings_target_ip_mappings"></a>The `ip_mappings` block contains:

* `ip_address` -
  (Output)
  The IP address assigned.

* `type` -
  (Output)
  The type of this IP address.

* `time_to_retire` -
  (Output)
  The due time for this IP to be retired.

<a name="nested_deployment_mappings_diffs"></a>The `diffs` block contains:

* `field` -
  (Output)

* `source_value` -

* `target_value` -
  (Output)

<a name="nested_deployment_tasks"></a>The `deployment_tasks` block contains:

  (Output)

<a name="nested_deployment_tasks_task"></a>The `task` block contains:

  (Output)

* `state` -
  (Output)
  The current state of the task.

* `start_time` -
  (Output)
  Task start time.

* `end_time` -
  (Output)
  Task end time.

* `error_message` -
  (Output)
  Optional error details if the task state is FAILED.

## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 60 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 60 minutes.

## Import


BlueGreenDeployment can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/blueGreenDeployments/{{blue_green_deployment_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{blue_green_deployment_id}}`
* `{{location}}/{{blue_green_deployment_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import BlueGreenDeployment using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    location = "<-required value->"
    blueGreenDeploymentId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_sql_blue_green_deployment.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import BlueGreenDeployment using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/blueGreenDeployments/{{blue_green_deployment_id}}"
  to = google_sql_blue_green_deployment.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), BlueGreenDeployment can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_sql_blue_green_deployment.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/blueGreenDeployments/{{blue_green_deployment_id}}
$ terraform import google_sql_blue_green_deployment.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{blue_green_deployment_id}}
$ terraform import google_sql_blue_green_deployment.default {{location}}/{{blue_green_deployment_id}}
```
